The worst that could happen is that the contract would continue executing without knowing that the external call failed. This could lead to inconsistent state and potential loss of funds for users involved in the transaction.

## Proof of Concept
The cases where `.CALL` function is used, but the return value is not stored in memory. These instances can potentially lead to errors if the return value is not properly checked.

**1. In the [depositETHAsset](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/YieldBox/blob/f5ad271b2dcab8b643b7cf622c2d6a128e109999/contracts/YieldBox.sol#L196-L215) function** [207](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/YieldBox/blob/f5ad271b2dcab8b643b7cf622c2d6a128e109999/contracts/YieldBox.sol#L207)

wrappedNative.deposit{ value: amount }();
```
The `.CALL` function is used to call the `deposit` function of the `wrappedNative` contract with `amount` as the value. However, the return value of the `.CALL` function is not stored in memory.

NOTE: This vulnerability relies on the team implementing an `onERC721Received()` function in Magnetar. As is currently written, attempts to exit oTAP positions via Magnetar will always revert as Magnetar cannot receive ERC721s, despite this being the clear intention of the function. ## Impact
1. An underflow in the `prod1` calculation within the `FullMath` contract can lead to contract failure and potential reverts, disrupting normal operations.

## Proof of Concept
There are two occurrences where subtractions are used that could potentially lead to an underflow. And these cases involve the use of the `sub` function, which may cause a revert if the result of the subtraction becomes negative.

}

The `emergencyWithdraw()` function calculates the minAmount of ETH received when withdrawing the total balance of stETH in the strategy as 0.5% of the total balance.

```
Presumably this meant to be a slippage protection but it just means you're willing to accept 0.5% of the amount of stETH as WETH (so for 1000 stETH in the strategy the `minAmount` of ETH acceptable would be 5 ETH). More likely this was mean to be:

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/modules/BaseTOFTLeverageModule.sol#L215

## Impact

Pathway for [`sendForLeverage`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L323) -> [`leverageDown`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L480) always fails if the `TapiocaOFT` or `mTapiocaOFT` holds the native token as underlying, i.e. [`erc20 == address(0)`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFTStorage.sol#L28). 
This results in loss of gas, airdropped amount, and burned TOFT on the sending side for the user. 
The failed message if retried will always fail and result in permanent loss for the user.

## Proof of Concept

TapiocaOFT/mTapiocaOFT is deployed with [erc20 being address(0)](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/TapiocaOFT.sol#L74) in case if it holds the native token as an underlying token.
However, it still allows anyone to execute the [`sendForLeverage`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L323) which always results in reverts when receiving the message.

The revert happens at [`IERC20(erc20).approve(externalData.swapper, amount);`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/master/contracts/tOFT/modules/BaseTOFTLeverageModule.sol#L215) since `address(0)` doesn't have an `approve` function.

The message if retried will just keep on reverting because of the same reason due to the way the `failedMessages` are stored, e.g. you can just retry the same exact payload.
This way anyone invoking this function will lose his TOFT tokens forever.

            ...
        }
    }
```

Manual Review

use the marketInterface.userBorrowPart(user) to get the user's borrow amount and

            if (share > _yieldBoxShares[from][ASSET_SIG]) {

Manual review.

        if (borrowed < startTVLInAsset) return minLiquidatorReward;

- When users wants to execute any operation through the Magnetar contract, the Magnetar contracts requires to have the user's approvals/permissions, that means, when the Magnetar contract executes something on behalf of the user, the Magnetar contract have already been granted permission/allowance on the called contract on the user's behalf.

- [When using the Magnetar contract to remove user assets from the Singularity market and use those assets to repay in a BigBang contract](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/modules/MagnetarMarketModule.sol#L568-L635), the Magnetar contract will receive the removed assets from the Singularity Market, grant ALL allowance to the BigBang contract in the YieldBox, and finally will call the BigBang.repay().

- The problem is that none of the two markets are checked to ensure that they are valid and supported contracts by the Protocol.

- This attack requires that an attacker creates a FakeBigBang contract (see Step 2 of the Coded PoC mini section!), and passes the address of this Fake BigBang contract as the address of the BigBang where the repayment will be done.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
All the ETH in the destination chain where `sendFrom()` is called is sent to the `refundAddress` in the `LzCallParams`. Thus, for `TapiocaOFT`s which have ETH as the underlying asset `erc`, all the funds will be lost if the `refundAddress` is an address other than the `TapiocaOFT`.

## Proof of Concept
`sendFrom()` uses the `msg.value` as native fees to LayerZero, being the excess sent refunded to the `refundAddress`. In `BaseTOFTOptionsModule`, `sendFromDestination()`, which is called when there was a `triggerSendFrom()` from a source chain which is delivered to the current chain, the value sent to the `sendFrom()` function is `address(this).balance`:
```
function sendFromDestination(bytes memory _payload) public {
    ...
    ISendFrom(address(this)).sendFrom{value: address(this).balance}(
        from,
        lzDstChainId,
        LzLib.addressToBytes32(from),
        amount,
        callParams
    );
    ...
}
```

This means that all the balance but the LayerZero message fee will be refunded to the `refundAddress` in the `callParams`, as can be seen in the `sendFrom()` function:

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/usd0/modules/USDOLeverageModule.sol#L54


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The vulnerability occurs in the initMultiHopBuy function, where ETH is transferred to the lzData.refundAddress, if initMultiHopBuy is called with a non-zero msg.value and then delegates to the multiHop function, the original msg.value will be lost in the new context. 
As a result, the ETH sent during initMultiHopBuy will not be transferred to the lzData.refundAddress, leaving the funds stranded in the contract.
 Here is the code where the vulnerability is occure : 

```solidity 
function initMultiHopBuy(
    address from,
    uint256 collateralAmount,
    uint256 borrowAmount,
    IUSDOBase.ILeverageSwapData calldata swapData,
    IUSDOBase.ILeverageLZData calldata lzData,
    IUSDOBase.ILeverageExternalContractsData calldata externalData,
    bytes calldata airdropAdapterParams,
    ICommonData.IApproval[] calldata approvals
) external payable {
    bytes32 senderBytes = LzLib.addressToBytes32(from);

    bytes memory lzPayload = abi.encode(
        PT_MARKET_MULTIHOP_BUY,
        senderBytes,
        from,
        collateralAmount,
        borrowAmount,
        swapData,
        lzData,
        externalData,
        approvals
    );

    _lzSend(
        lzData.lzSrcChainId,
        lzPayload,
        payable(lzData.refundAddress),
        lzData.zroPaymentAddress,
        airdropAdapterParams,
        msg.value
    );
    emit SendToChain(lzData.lzSrcChainId, msg.sender, senderBytes, 0);
}

```

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L1025-L1049


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When calling [MagnetarV2._permit(...)](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L1025-L1049) through invoking a permit (or permit all) action via [MagnetarV2.burst(...)](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L192-L715), one can also execute other calls than `ERC20.permit(...)` due to the following reasons / under the following constraints:
* The `target` address can be chosen freely, can be any contract, asset, token, NFT, etc.
* The function selector in `actionCalldata` is not checked, i.e. not required to be `ERC20.permit(...)`
* The first parameter in the encoded `actionCalldata` [**must** be equal to `msg.sender`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L1036)
* The length of the `actionCalldata` should match the length of an encoded call to `ERC20.permit(...)` to avoid issues on [`abi.decode(...)`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L1032-L1035)

Given this information, an attacker can easily craft calls to give him approval for any assets held by the `MagnetarV2` contract or directly invoke a transfer. issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/usd0/modules/USDOOptionsModule.sol#L189


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The vulnerability occure in the exercise and exerciseInternal functions when delegating the call to an external module. The contract allows an external module to be called, and in the process, the contract credits the contract with an amount of tokens (optionsData.paymentTokenAmount), the contract does not ensure that this amount is returned if the external call to the module reverts, In the exercise function, the contract checks if the credited tokens are enough to cover the payment (balanceAfter - balanceBefore >= optionsData.paymentTokenAmount). If there are enough tokens, the contract forwards them to the caller, if the external module call reverts and the credited tokens are not enough, the contract does not return the excess tokens to the caller. This can lead to a loss of funds for the contract owner.

## Proof of Concept


 this vulnerability is leading to  loss of funds for the contract owner if an attacker exploit it. The problem If the external module call reverts and the credited tokens are not enough to cover the payment, the contract does not return the excess tokens to the caller optionsData.from

## Tools Used
Manual review 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
I recommend to Ensure Proper Handling of Credited Tokens all this can done by ensure proper handling of credited tokens. Specifically, the contract should refund the excess tokens to the caller if the external module call reverts and the credited tokens are not used entirely.

The contract can implement a check to ensure that the credited tokens are used entirely in the external module call. If not, any excess tokens should be returned to the caller before the contract reverts due to the external call.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L129


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `swapper` contract address cannot be updated as intended because there exists no logic to approve the new `swapper` contract.

## Proof of Concept
The `AaveStrategy.swapper` contract address is used to swap `rewardToken`s, and for that reason is approved by the strategy contract to spend `rewardToken`s in the constructor.

```solidity
// constructor()
rewardToken.approve(_multiSwapper, type(uint256).max);
```

There is a function to update the `swapper` address, but it fails to include the necessary approvals for the updated contract address to function correctly.

```solidity
function setMultiSwapper(address _swapper) external onlyOwner {
	emit MultiSwapper(address(swapper), _swapper);
	swapper = ISwapper(_swapper);
}
```

As a result, it's impossible for the `swapper` address to be updated while remaining functional.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It's recommended that an approval to the new `swapper` is included in `setMultiSwapper`.


## Assessed type

ERC20

L​ack of ​chainID​ validation allows signatures to be reused across forks
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L263-L272


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

MarketERC20​ implements the draft ERC 2612 via the ERC20Permit​ contract it inherits from. This allows a third party to transmit a signature from a token holder that modifies the ERC20 allowance for a particular user. These signatures used in calls to permit​ in ​ERC20Permit​ do not account for chainsplits. The ​chainID​ is included in the domain separator. However, it is not updatable and not included in the signed data as part of the permit​ call. As a result, if the chain forks after deployment, the signed message may be considered valid on both forks.

## Proof of Concept

Bob has a wallet holding ​tokens​. An EIP is included in an upcoming hard fork that has split the community. After the hard fork, a significant user base remains on the old chain. On the new chain, Bob approves Alice to spend some tokens via a call to permit​. Alice, operating on both chains, replays the ​permit​ call on the old chain and is able to steal some of Bob’s tokens.

## Tools Used

Manual review + in-house tool

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Short term, include the chainID​ opcode in the permit​ schema. This will make replay attacks impossible in the event of a post-deployment hard fork. Long term, document and carefully review any signature schemas, including their robustness to replay on different wallets, contracts, and blockchains. Make sure users are aware of signing best practices and the danger of signing messages from untrusted sources.


## Assessed type

Access Control

## Impact
GlpStrategy is entirely non-functional due to lack of token approvals.

## Proof of Concept
Several functions called require approval of tokens for execution to proceed. For example, in `_vestByGlp`, we call `glpVester.deposit`, which executes a `safeTransferFrom`, obviously requiring approval to succeed.

```solidity
// _vestByGlp()
glpVester.deposit(vestable);

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionLiquidityProvision.sol#L297-L329
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionLiquidityProvision.sol#L247


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When the OLP owner unregisters a Singularity, locked positions cannot be unlocked, which causes token loss.

## Proof of Concept
In `unregisterSingularity()` of TapiocaOptionLiquidityProvision.sol, the owner can unregister a Singularity. Currently, `activeSingularities` is removed for the specific Singularity. This is problematic if called when there are locked positions.

When a position is locked, the `_amount` is added to `activeSingularities[_singularity].totalDeposited`
```
function lock(
    address _to,
    IERC20 _singularity,
    uint128 _lockDuration,
    uint128 _amount
    ) external returns (uint256 tokenId) {
    ...
    activeSingularities[_singularity].totalDeposited += _amount;

    ..
}
```

Thus, if a Singularity is unregistered, `activeSingularities[singularity].totalDeposited` becomes `0`, which means any subsequent calls to `unlock()` will cause an underflow. 
```
function unlock(
	uint256 _tokenId,
	IERC20 _singularity,
	address _to
) external returns (uint256 sharesOut) {
	...
	activeSingularities[_singularity].totalDeposited -= lockPosition.amount;
	...
}
```

There is no way to fix this accounting store, so this results in permanently locked positions.

## Tools Used
Eyeballs

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider checking if `activeSingularities[singularity].totalDeposited == 0` before unregistering.






## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Frozen underlying assets of the `TapiocaOFT`s if there is a blockchain fork. Wrapping will also not be possible anymore both in `mTapiocaOFT`s and `TapiocaOFT`s.

## Proof of Concept
`TapiocaOFT`s may be wrapped and unwrapped for the underlying asset in the host chain (native chain for this asset). Then, as `TapiocaOFT` and `mTapiocaOFT` are deployed to several chains, in order to be able to wrap/unwrap the underlying asset only in the chain where the asset is native, the `hostChainId` is stored in the constructor and is compared against the `block.chainid` on wrap/unwrap operations, in the modifier `onlyHostChain`.

Thus, if a host blockchain is forked, the chain id will change and the wrap/unwrap operations will always revert. Given that in the natspec documentation of the `_hostChainID` parameter of the constructor of `TapiocaOFT` and `mTapiocaOFT` it mentions that this id is the LayerZero id instead, this is likely a mistake from the development team.

# Vulnerability details

## Summary
AAVEStrategy won't generate the expected rewards due to AAVE's liquidity mining program being no longer active.

## Vulnerability Detail
Tapioca's AAVEStrategy is designed to interact with AAVE's V2, not AAVE's latest V3. Considering this, the strategy aims not only at benefiting from regular AAVE rewards generated by depositing into the protocol as a liquidity provider, but also at obtaining rewards from [AAVE's liquidity mining program](https://docs.aave.com/developers/v/2.0/guides/liquidity-mining). We can see how both `compoundAmount()` and `compound()` functions try to claim stkAAVE, convert it to AAVE and then swap to `wrappedNative` in order to increase the strategy's balance.

The problem with this approach is that AAVE's liquidity mining program finished on Sun May 22 2022 19:00:28 GMT+0200. The [IncentivesController](https://etherscan.io/address/0xd784927Ff2f95ba542BfC824c8a8a98F3495f6b5#code) contract has a [DISTRIBUTION_END](https://docs.aave.com/developers/v/2.0/guides/liquidity-mining#getdistributionend) method which returns the exact UNIX timestamp where the distribution period of incentives finalizes. This means that since Sun may 22 2022 19:00:28 GMT+0200, no more liquidity mining rewards have been generated. Although the strategy can still generate profits by only depositing into AAVE, the goal of the strategy is clearly to benefit from the liquidity mining rewards, which clearly renders the strategy unusable.

High, the strategy won't work as intended and no rewards from liquidity mining will be generated.

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L721-L739
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLendingCommon.sol#L83-L98


# Vulnerability details

## Impact and Details
In `_liquidateUser()/_orderBookLiquidation()`, the internal `_repay()` function is never called, hence indicating that liquidator USDO balance is not burnt to repay borrower's CDP positions. 

While it is true they only receive liquidation incentive based on current exchange rates, it essentially means that the liquidation mechanism is free of charge, since liquidator's do not risk their own CDP positions.

Depending on collateral type, this can cause the Tapioca's BigBang/Singularity markets to incur huge losses in the form of paying profits for liquidator's for free.

- Liquidator's USDO balance is not updated (burned) based on current exchange rate, allowing liquidator's to arbritrage, by choosing exchange rates that favor them to liquidate, they can drain collateral in the form of rewards paid by Tapioca protocol due to liquidation bonuses
- This allows liquidators to always keep a healthy CDP position by redepositing earned rewards and borrow more USDO
- This also opens up for malicious borrowers to liquidate their own positions to get liquidation bonus and then redeposit, allowing them to permanently prevent positions from liquidation and incur bad debt for Singularity and BigBang markets due to payment of liquidation bonuses.

## Tools Used
Manual Analysis

## Recommendation
Call the internal `_repay()` function when liquidator's liquidate borrower's CDP position under maximum LTV ratio via `liquidate()` function. This forces liquidators to burn their EUSD (signifying loss)

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/yearn/YearnStrategy.sol#L142-L143


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
An overflow in the `toWithdraw` amount can lead to incorrect token transfer calculations, potentially causing a loss of funds if the wrong amount is withdrawn from the Yearn Vault.

## Proof of Concept
There is one instance of code that performs downcasting, which could potentially lead to an overflow.
The vulnerable code is located in the `_withdraw` function.

[L142-L143](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/yearn/YearnStrategy.sol#L142-L143)

```solidity
            uint256 toWithdraw = (((amount - queued) *
                (10 ** vault.decimals())) / pricePerShare);
```
In the `_withdraw` function, the contract calculates the `toWithdraw` amount by subtracting the `queued` balance from the specified `amount`. It then multiplies the result by `(10 ** vault.decimals())` and divides it by `pricePerShare`. This multiplication with `(10 ** vault.decimals())` is a downcasting operation and can lead to an overflow if `vault.decimals()` is set to a value that causes the result to exceed the maximum representable value for the data type.

If `vault.decimals()` is set to a large value, the multiplication operation `((amount - queued) * (10 ** vault.decimals()))` could exceed the maximum value representable by `uint256`, leading to an overflow. As a result, the calculated `toWithdraw` amount would become incorrect, potentially leading to unintended behavior or reverting transactions that rely on the proper `toWithdraw` value.

A scenario to demonstrate the potential overflow vulnerability in the `_withdraw` function of the YearnStrategy smart contract.

Assume the following values:
- `amount` is set to 1000.
- `queued` is set to 900.
- `vault.decimals()` is set to 20.

Attackers can exploit this flaw to steal tokens from the contract or initiate unauthorized transfers.

## Proof of Concept
Arbitrary bytes are decoded from the `data` parameter of external functions.

function uniswapV3SwapCallback(
    int256 /* amount0Delta */,
    int256 /* amount1Delta */,
    bytes calldata data
) external {
    require(msg.sender == address(gmxWethPool), "Not the pool");
    uint256 amount = abi.decode(data, (uint256));
    gmx.safeTransfer(address(gmxWethPool), amount);
}
```
- The `uniswapV3SwapCallback` function takes three arguments, but only `bytes calldata data` is used in this function.
- The `data` parameter is expected to be arbitrary bytes.
- The function uses `abi.decode(data, (uint256))` to decode the arbitrary bytes into a `uint256` value, stored in the `amount` variable.
- The decoded `amount` is subsequently used in a `safeTransfer` function call to transfer `amount` tokens of the `gmx` token to the address of the `gmxWethPool` contract.
- The function uses the `abi.decode` function to decode the data parameter. This function is not overflow-safe, which means that it could overflow if the value of the data parameter is too large.
- The function uses the `gmx.safeTransfer` function to transfer tokens. This function is not overflow-safe, which means that it could overflow if the value of the amount parameter is too large.

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L790-L796


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

During the liquidation process the function `updateBorrowAndCollateralShare` calls the function `computeClosingFactor` to compute how much part of the debt can be liquidated. The problem is that due to an error, this function might return zero when it should not, see PoC.

## Proof of Concept

The function at some point makes the following comparison:

```solidity
// @audit-info collateralizationRate * USD_Value_Collateral.
uint256 liquidationStartsAt = (collateralPartInAssetScaled * collateralizationRate) / (10 ** ratesPrecision);

// @audit-issue It should convert this to real debt before.
if (borrowPartScaled < liquidationStartsAt) return 0;
```

The variable `liquidationStartsAt` represents the max amount of debt a user can have before a liquidation can start on its position. The issue is that `borrowPartScaled` is not the actual debt of the user but just its part of the total debt. Because `borrowPartScaled` will always be smaller than the real debt, this function might return zero when the position is indeed open to liquidation.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Transform `borrowPartScaled` to the real debt before and use the result in the comparison. To transform it to the real debt, do the following:

```solidity
uint256 realDebt = (borrowPart * totalBorrow.elastic) / (totalBorrow.base);
```





## Assessed type

Other

Faulty allowance check allows to steal yieldbox tokens from anyone
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLCollateral.sol#L27
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLendingCommon.sol#L23


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Yieldbox tokens can be stolen from any user.

## Proof of Concept
In `SGLCollateral.addCollateral`, we have an `allowedBorrow` check which ensures that the caller has been approved by `from` for the amount of `shares` passed.

```solidity
function addCollateral(
	address from,
	address to,
	bool skim,
	uint256 amount,
	uint256 share
) public notPaused allowedBorrow(from, share) { 
```

The flaw in this use is that as we can see in `_addCollateral`, which is called with the provided params, if `share` is passed as 0, we simply compute `share` from `amount`.

```solidity
function _addCollateral(
	address from,
	address to,
	bool skim,
	uint256 amount,
	uint256 share
) internal {
	if (share == 0) {
		share = yieldBox.toShare(collateralId, amount, false);
	}
```

As a result, anyone call `Singularity.addCollateral` with any valid `from` address, `share` as 0, and `amount` as the total amount that `from` has in Yieldbox, passing their own address as `to`. The attacker can then remove the collateral with `Singularity.removeCollateral`, transferring the tokens from Yieldbox to themselves.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

It's necessary that the conversion from amount to shares is done prior to checking whether the amount of shares to be used has been allowed.


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Possible to front-run `broker` filling use function `brokerClaim`.
This leads to the loss of contract management.

## Proof of Concept
Let's consider `oTAP` (`aoTAP` has the same problem).
* We're creating contract.
* Next we need to set `broker`. But the enemy may front-run our transaction and call `brokerClaim()` before us. This leads to the fact that the criminal gets access to the main functions of the contract.
* This front-run case broke `TapiocaOptionBroker` because it need to be broker for the `oTAP`.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Rewrite this function to be called by only owner. I.e. only Owner can set value.

MEV

issues.title: `MagnetarMarketModule.depositRepayAndRemoveCollateralFromMarket(...)` can be invoked with other user's tokens
Incorrect american option implementation
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L351-L409


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

Possible to get tokens every week, while option is not expired. This is strongly incorrect behavior. Because these options are american -- https://docs.tapioca.xyz/tapioca/token-economy/dso-dao-share-options#whats-an-american-style-call-option
But main idea of options -- possibility to execute only once. 
Here we can execute this as many as possible. 


## Proof of Concept
Let's consider `TapiocaOptionBroker.sol` contract.
* We got option token (tokenId from OTAP).
* We lock this token.
* We decided to execute this token -- we call `exerciseOption`
Here some standard checks happens,
Next: 

eligible amount calculated
```
uint256 eligibleTapAmount = muldiv(
            tOLPLockPosition.amount,
            gaugeTotalForEpoch,
            tOLP.getTotalPoolDeposited(tOLPLockPosition.sglAssetID)
        );
``` 

Calculated amount to option owner:
```
        eligibleTapAmount -= oTAPCalls[_oTAPTokenID][cachedEpoch]; // Subtract already exercised amount
        require(eligibleTapAmount >= _tapAmount, "tOB: Too high");

        uint256 chosenAmount = _tapAmount == 0 ? eligibleTapAmount : _tapAmount;
        require(chosenAmount >= 1e18, "tOB: Too low");
        oTAPCalls[_oTAPTokenID][cachedEpoch] += chosenAmount;
```

Tokens transferred to user:

```
_processOTCDeal(
            _paymentToken,
            paymentTokenOracle,
            chosenAmount,
            oTAPPosition.discount
        );
```

From this moment option is expired, but in reality we can execute this option once again on a next week.

## Tools Used

Manual review


## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Either burn expired option at the end of execution flow, or add flag -- `executed`


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: Calling `claimAndSendRewards` function of the `twTap` contract without verifying if `twTap` is a trusted and secure contract.

Attacker can use Magnetar contract to extract assets from user's accounts and deposit them into the YieldBox, and by using a fake market contract it can transfer the deposited assets in the YieldBox to an address of his own
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/modules/MagnetarMarketModule.sol#L212-L254


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
- User's assets can be extracted from their accounts before they are deposited into the YieldBox by using the Magnetar contract, and by using a fake market contract, an attacker can transfer those assets to an address of his own. 

## Proof of Concept
- Users can use the [`Magnetar::depositRepayAndRemoveCollateralFromMarket()`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/Magnetar/MagnetarV2.sol#L802-L838) function to deposit asset to YieldBox, repay on a market, remove collateral and withdraw, but before the function can be executed, the users need to grant allowance to the Magnetar contract to spend the asset tokens on their behalf.
- The depositRepayAndRemoveCollateralFromMarket() function basically extracts the asset tokens from the users account, deposit them into the YieldBox and then it can repay the user's debt using those deposited assets, also it can remove collateral from the market and withdraw it to his account on any supported chain by the protocol.

- **The problem is** that the depositRepayAndRemoveCollateralFromMarket() function can be exploited by an attacker because it lacks validation to check if the assets are going to be extracted from the `user` address (which is a parameter) or from the caller (msg.sender), and also lacks validation to verify if the provided `market` address is a legit, suported market by the protocol.
  - These two flaws in combination allows attackers to steal user's assets from their accounts by using the Magnetar contract.

### Practical Example:

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The init function don't have access control and anyone can execute it. Because of this, 
the attacker can front-run the init function and designate itself as owner by manipulating the input parameters. One of the functions that it can access as owner is refreshPenroseFees where it can transfer the fees to the attacker or msg.sender

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L466-L480
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L369-L376


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

In `twTAP.sol` contract you may lock a bit of tapOFT values to participate in farming.
So, after locking you may withdraw every week a bit of tokens.
And after lock timeout expire you can withdraw TAP tokens.
But `_requireClaimPermission` and `releaseTap` implemented in such way -- that anyone can return your money back to you. And from this moment you stop receive any additional tokens.
This is incorrect behavior.

## Proof of Concept

* `twTAP` contract created
* you got tapOFT tokens, and decided to lock them for a month
* so you call `participate` function, and get nft -- `tokenId`
* then you (or someone calls) `claimRewards` to get tokens
* after locking period you may leave tokens on the contract or withdraw them and stop receiving rewards -- this step can be called by anyone

```
    function releaseTap(uint256 _tokenId, address _to) external {
        _requireClaimPermission(_to, _tokenId);
        _releaseTap(_tokenId, _to);
    }

    function _requireClaimPermission(
        address _to,
        uint256 _tokenId
    ) internal view {
        address tokenOwner = ownerOf(_tokenId);
        require(
            msg.sender == tokenOwner ||
                _to == tokenOwner || // <- here anyone can close position for you,
                isApprovedForAll(tokenOwner, msg.sender) ||
                getApproved(_tokenId) == msg.sender,
            "twTAP: cannot claim"
        );
    }
```

So if you have detractors -- they may close your position and you won't get additional rewards.


This isn't a good practice, better add permit functionality, and if you don't have enough fee you man sign transaction with Permit.

## Tools Used

Manual review

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/master/contracts/lido/LidoEthStrategy.sol#L108


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`LidoEthStrategy` contract is exposed to sandwich attack, if `emergencyWithdraw` is called because the slippage is not calculated correctly.

## Proof of Concept
Let's imagine that protocol needs to call `emergencyWithdraw` for unexpected reasons.

The issue is that because the `minAmount` calculation is incorrect, a malicious user may listen to mempool and sandwich attack to gain profit (make protocol lose money) from the `emergencyWithdraw` call.
```solidity
  function emergencyWithdraw() external onlyOwner returns (uint256 result) {
    compound("");

    uint256 toWithdraw = stEth.balanceOf(address(this));
    uint256 minAmount = (toWithdraw * 50) / 10_000; //0.5% @audit - Incorrectly calculated
    result = curveStEthPool.exchange(1, 0, toWithdraw, minAmount);

    INative(address(wrappedNative)).deposit{ value: result }();
  }
```

### Example
Let's say that the `toWithdraw` amount is 100 stETH
This means that `minAmount` is going to be (100 * 50 / 10000) => 0.5 stETH.
Malicious user can easily sandwich attack the `emergencyWithdraw` function to cause lost funds for the protocol.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
If it was intended to have 0.5% slippage, update the `minAmount` calculation to following:
```solidity
    uint256 minAmount = toWithdraw - (toWithdraw * 50) / 10_000;
```


## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
One of the settings for the big bang market is called the debtStartPoint. it is set during contract initialization and once set it is not modifiable afterwards. 

this variables plays a key part during interest accrual. any time a user attempts to repay a loan or liquidate a position the accrue function is triggered. this in turn attempts to update the debt rate via this code block:

            //update debt rate
        uint256 annumDebtRate = getDebtRate();
        _accrueInfo.debtRate = uint64(annumDebtRate / 31536000); //per second


the getDebtRate function will then run this code block:

        // @audit if this debtstart point is set too high either by mistake or not
        // then code below will revert with underflow
        uint256 debtPercentage = ((_currentDebt - debtStartPoint) *
            DEBT_PRECISION) / (_maxDebtPoint - debtStartPoint);
        uint256 debt = ((maxDebtRate - minDebtRate) * debtPercentage) /
            DEBT_PRECISION +
            minDebtRate;

Now the problem manifests in the code above. if the debtStartPoint is set to a very large amount, then as long as current total borrowings in system are below this amount, the calculate will underflow and force a revert.

The consequence of this is the system market will be extremely unstable up to the point where total borrowing reach that set debtstartpoint which like mentioned earlier, if set to an arbitrarily large number, could be a very distant time in the future. untill that point is reached, any collateral added by users will by locked in contract. not only that but since liquidations also trigger the function, they too will be disabled. 

Based on that I rate the impact of this on the bigbang market as severe.

issues.title: Possible to manipulate Uniswap V3 oracle price
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/oracle/utils/UniswapUtils.sol#L16-L18


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

## Proof of Concept
Because protocol will be deployed to ETH main net, it's possible to manipulate at least two blocks.
So, possible to shift price significantly.
Let's refer to https://blog.uniswap.org/uniswap-v3-oracles#fn-2, here told:
`Two block Uniswap v3 TWAP oracle manipulation is still prohibitively expensive on top pairs in a PoS environment. Potential manipulators need to move the price by 71,721,000,000,000% for a single block to change the 30-min TWAP oracle price by 20%, which requires sourcing an infeasible amount of assets and losing a massive amount of it to fees`
Another one paper: https://basin.exchange/multi-flow-pump.pdf, here in figure 1 shown Multi-Block MEV Occurrences Per Year By Validator Ownership Percent.  

Possible attack vector:

Robber produces two or three blocks in row, 
At the first block he buys all tokens from V3 exchange, 
At the second and at the third block he forbid any other participants to make trade on this exchange, 
And in these blocks robber makes trade with incorrect price to fill UniswapV3 trade history and increase TWAP. 
At the end of third block he returns funds back and normalize price.

So, when Oracle will be requested price with small TWAP (for example 5 minutes) it may get incorrect price.

This could be fixed by a large interval.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Increase min twap rate from 5 minutes to 15 minutes


## Assessed type

Uniswap

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

If price drops fast and significantly here might be possible case, when borrowed amount with borrow interest will be bigger than whole user's collateral amount. (i.e. -- `borrow + borrowFee > collateral / ExcahngeRate`). 
This case might be happened if in the swap pool hasn't enough liquidity.
In such case transaction will be reverted, because `returnedShare < borrowShare`


## Proof of Concept
Let's go throw liquidation logic.
Let's consider `BigBand#_liquidateUser` function,
Here we call `_updateBorrowAndCollateralShare` which returns borrowAmount to repay to protocol with collateral amount to sell.
Next we sell all `collateralShare` to receive borrow assert `returnedShare`, and in function `_extractLiquidationFees` we subtracts: `returnedShare - borrowShare` to calculate fees to liquidator and protocol. But here `returnedShare` might be less than `borrowShare` due to fast price moves or small liquidity amount.

## Tools Used

Manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

in Function `_extractLiquidationFees` exit if `borrowShare > returnedShare`

Math

issues.title: BaseTOFT._wrap() never spends any allowance from BaseTOFT, as a result, a user can mint more TapiocaOFT tokens than allowed.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L348-L361


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.
BaseTOFT._wrap() only checks that there is enough allownace for msg.sender to wrap the ERC20 token from the ``_fromAddress``. However, such allowance is never spent, as a result, the allowance can be used indefinitely by the spender.  

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

Consider the case that ``erc20 != address(0)``, and user address(222) calls ``TapiocaOFT.wrap()`` to wrap erc20 tokens from ``_fromAddress``. 

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/TapiocaOFT.sol#L69-L79](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/TapiocaOFT.sol#L69-L79)

However, when it calls BaseTOFT._wrap(), the allowance of BaseTOFT is checked but never spent - what is spent is the allowance for erc20 not for BaseTOFT. 

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L348-L361](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/BaseTOFT.sol#L348-L361)

The following POC code shows that address(111) approves address(222) only 100,000 allowance for the TapiocaOFT tokens, but address(222) will never spend this allowance for TapiocaOFT (although it will spend the allowance for tokenA). This means, a malicious user can mint more TapiocaOFT tokens from ``_fromAddress`` than allowed by TapiocaOFT.allowance(address(111), address(222)). In our example, while 
TapiocaOFT.allowance(address(111), address(222)) = 100,000, but 300,000 TapiocaOFT tokens are minted by address(222).

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/Singularity.sol#L181-L195


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Singularity.sol can be destructed and funds may be stolen from the contract.

## Proof of Concept
The 'execute' function in Singularity.sol executes the batched calls to singularity market and takes An array encoded call data as param, now this function delegates the call to modules that were passed in calls array, the array call is the encoded calldata to pass, so function signature + parameters which is supposed to delegate the call to the following modules that was also mentioned inside the enum 
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/Singularity.sol#L45-L51
but before delegating the call there is no check whether the call is delegated to the modules or not, which might result in an adversary delegating the call to his malicious contact and performing the selfdestruct destroying the contract and he may also steal the funds of the singularity market because it hands over the execution control to the malicious entity, because the entire isolated market and maybe user funds is at risk of being lost so giving it high severity.
selfdestruct has been deprecated from version 0.8.18 but it can still be used.

## Tools Used
Manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make sure the calls are delegating to the right place i.e., targeting the function selectors of modules and delegation should strictly not be allowed anywhere else.



## Assessed type

call/delegatecall

issues.title: Function `compound` from `AaveStrategy.sol` will revert 100% making withdrawing impossible
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L163-L165


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Function `compound` is used almost every time `emergencyWithdraw` or `_withdraw`, but it will revert 100% of the time it gets called, which will make the withdrawing impossible and the user's funds stuck in the contract.

## Proof of Concept
`compound` tries to claim and unclaimed rewards from the `incentivesController` and after that it call `stakersCooldowns` on the `stakedRewardToken` 
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L163-L165
trying to check the current cooldown. The problem relies in the fact that the function `stakersCooldowns` will return 2 variables and not one, it will return an uint40 timestamp variable and a uint216 amount variable as can be seen here 
https://etherscan.io/address/0x4da27a545c0c5B758a6BA100e3a049001de870f5#readProxyContract#F47
, but in the `AaveStrategy.sol` it assumes and expects only one uint256 variable, which will not be the case. Since the `stakersCooldowns` function returns 2 variables and the `compound` function expects only one, the transaction will revert all the time it will be called, which will make withdrawing funds from the contract impossible.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Since the function `stakersCooldowns` returns a tuple, create two memory variables and assert those values to those two memory variables instead of only one.


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: `setMultiSwapper` in `AaveStrategy.sol` does not update the allowance to the new address set which will make funds be stuck in the contract
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L129-L132


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The function `setMultiSwapper` can be called by the owner to change the address of the swapper used in the contract, but it doesn't also `approve` the `rewardToken` to the new address, which will make the function that calls `compound` revert.

## Proof of Concept
The function that calls `compound` are `emergencyWithdraw` and `_withdraw` which will try to swap the `rewardToken` to `wrappedNative`, but if the address of the swapper will be changed by the user calling `setMultiSwapper` because it will need to use another swapper than intended, the `swap` function will revert all the time, because the new address of the swapper will not have any allowance of the `rewardToken` making the transaction fail. This means that anytime the owner tries to `emergencyWithdraw` or a user tries to `_withdraw` the transaction will revert and funds will be stuck in the contract if something happened and first swapper used in the constructor is not usable anymore.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Approve the `rewardToken` to the new address of the swapper in the `setMultiSwapper`.


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: `_sellGmx` in `GlpStrategy.sol` can transfer more funds to the UniswapV3 pool than needed, funds which will be lost
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/glp/GlpStrategy.sol#L86-L94


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The function `_sellGmx` uses the UniswapV3 GMX/ETH pool to sell GMX and buy WETH, but the `uniswapV3SwapCallback` can transfer more funds to the pool than it needs too, funds which will be lost in the UniswapV3 pool.

## Proof of Concept
`_sellGmx` calls the `swap` function with the next arguments 
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/glp/GlpStrategy.sol#L324-L330
`zeroForOne` argument being all the time false, which means that it will sell GMX to buy WETH. The `swap` function on the UniswapV3 pool does some calculations and asserts `amount0`, which in our case will be the amount of WETH tokens that the contract will get, and `amount1` which is the amount of GMX the contract needs to transfer in the `uniswapV3SwapCallback`. The `amount1` that needs to be transferred is not always equal to the amount specified in the `swap` function, as you can see in the UniswapV3 pool code https://arbiscan.io/address/0x80A9ae39310abf666A87C743d6ebBD0E8C42158E#code#F1#L770
in our case `amount1` will be equal to `amountSpecified - state.amountSpecifiedRemaining` which can be less most of the time than the `amountSpecified`. After the calculations the pool calls the callback function on `GlpStrategy.sol` and expects that the `balance1` to be equal or greater to `balance1Before` + `amount1`
https://arbiscan.io/address/0x80A9ae39310abf666A87C743d6ebBD0E8C42158E#code#F1#L784
but `uniswapV3SwapCallback` function transfers the amount of GMX specified in the swap function, instead of transferring the `amount1` that the pool needs for the require statement to pass, which most of the time will be a bigger value, funds that will remain in the UniswapV3 contract for no reason.

The function `_sendToken` is called on `rebalance` to perform the rebalance operation by the owner which will transfer native token or the underlying ERC20 for a specific tOFT token to other chains. This function uses the `router` from Stargate to transfer the tokens, but the implementation of the `swap` is done wrong which will make the tokens to be lost.

## Proof of Concept
`_sendToken` calls Stargate's router `swap` function with the all the parameters needed as can be seen here https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/Balancer.sol#L322-L332, but the problem relies that the destination address is computed by calling `abi.encode(connectedOFTs[_oft][_dstChainId].dstOft)` instead of the `abi.encodePacked(connectedOFTs[_oft][_dstChainId].dstOft)` https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/Balancer.sol#L316-L318.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `MagnetarV2.sol` contract has a method that allows users to permit ERC20 tokens in other parts of the Tapioca ecosystem.

This method has a vulnerability where the function signature of the external call isn't checked. The end result is that a malicious user can call `permit` but pass in an arbitrary function signature to call an arbitrary method on an arbitrary contract from the context of the Magnetar contract. There is some restriction on the first argument of the calldata, but this exploit path can be used set the allowance of any user for the Magnetar YieldBox balance. The malicious user can effectively steal the yield box balance of Magnetar.

This is just one attack avenue and is most destructive when used in combination with another vulnerability I've reported where `depositRepayAndRemoveCollateralFromMarket` doesn't validate the sender. A malicious user can pull assets from other users into the Magnetar YieldBox using that exploit path and then follow up with the exploit path detailed below to steal those assets (for themselves, rather than just draining the user's balance).

Like I stated above, since a malicious user can call arbitrary contracts and methods from the context of the Magnetar contract, other exploit paths are probably also possible (although it's worth noting that the restriction on the first calldata parameter does limit potential avenues).

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `MagnetarV2.sol` contract is a helper contract that allows users to interact with other parts of the Tapioca ecosystem. In order for Magnetar to be able to perform actions on behalf of a user, the user has to approve the contract as an approved spender (or equivalent) of the relevant tokens in the part of the Tapioca ecosystem the user wants to interact with.

In order to avoid abuse, many of the actions that Magnetar can perform are protected by a check that the owner of the position/token needs to be the `msg.sender` of the user interacting with Magnetar. However, there are some methods that are callable through Magnetar that don't have this check. This allows a malicious user to use approvals other users have made to Magnetar to steal their underlying tokens.

```
    function _checkSender(address _from) internal view {
        require(_from == msg.sender, "MagnetarV2: operator not approved");
    }

issues.title: SGLLiquidation's `liquidate` function will revert if trying to liquidate multiple users at the same time --> protocol may become insolvent.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLiquidation.sol#L33
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLiquidation.sol#L381
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/master/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLiquidation.sol#L338-L350


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
SGLLiquidation's `liquidate` function will revert if trying to liquidate multiple users at the same time --> protocol may become insolvent. (due to using the same swap data)

## Proof of Concept
- When the `liquidate` function is called, it'll invoke `_closedLiquidation`, which will loop through to liquidate each user's position. However, there's `swapData` that doesn't get loop through or split, but instead the whole `swapData` gets passed in to `_liquidateUser` as `dexData`
--> This means that in each of the iterations to execute `_liquidateUser` , the swap data will get executed each time.

```solidity
        ISwapper.SwapData memory swapData = swapper.buildSwapData(
            collateralId,
            assetId,
            0,
            collateralShare,
            true,
            true
        );
        swapper.swap(swapData, minAssetAmount, address(this), "");
```

This can potentially lead to liquidation reverts for latter liquidations --> potentially leading to protocol insolvency.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
- Accept swap data as `bytes[]` instead (let each swap data item be executed in each liquidate iteration)


## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
An attacker can force USDO token burn on contracts that hold USDO and have non-zero USDO token approvals to the USDO contract (note: it's very common that contracts approve `type(uint).max`) -- griefing those contracts.

## Proof of Concept
Anyone can call `flashloan` to any `receiver` address. Normally, the `msg.sender` needs to be the one to repay the flashloaned amount + fee. However, USDO implementation tries to burn from the `receiver` address instead. 

This means an attacker can initiate the `flashloan` to a contract as `receiver` that holds USDO and have non-zero approval (and also implement `onFlashLoan` function). 
--> `fee` will be additionally burned from the receiver

## Tools Used
Manual Review

- Burn from `msg.sender` instead of the `receiver`

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/balancer/BalancerStrategy.sol#L202-L205


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
BalancerStrategy `withdraw` function uses incorrect token amounts (using LP token amounts instead of wrapped native in the calculation). 

## Proof of Concept
- In the `_withdraw` function , the variable `pricePerShare` holds the conversion rate between BPT tokens and the wrapped native tokens.
  --> The `toWithdraw` amount corresponds to the BPT token amount to withdraw (dividing the wrapped asset amount by the rate above)
  --> The `_vaultWithdraw` function then takes the BPT token amounts to withdraw
  --> However, if we look at the `_vaultWithdraw` function, the argument `amount` is used as the wrapped native token amount (it is used as the `minAmountOut` for the wrapped native token)

--> This means the slippage control will be incorrectly passed on --> either leading to 
- tx reverts, OR
- very bad slippage control --> can be MEV attacked

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Either update the logic to `_vaultWithdraw` to take in the amount of BPT tokens to withdraw, or update the logic in the `_withdraw` function to pass in the correct `amount` value.

MEV

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/lido/LidoEthStrategy.sol#L118-L125


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
LidoEthStrategy._currentBalance can be manipulated by changing price in curve pool. This allows attacker to withdraw more funds.

## Proof of Concept
`LidoEthStrategy._currentBalance` is used to know how many eth is controlled by startegy.
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/lido/LidoEthStrategy.sol#L118-L125
```solidity
    function _currentBalance() internal view override returns (uint256 amount) {
        uint256 stEthBalance = stEth.balanceOf(address(this));
        uint256 calcEth = stEthBalance > 0
            ? curveStEthPool.get_dy(1, 0, stEthBalance)
            : 0;
        uint256 queued = wrappedNative.balanceOf(address(this));
        return calcEth + queued;
    }
```
So when `stEthBalance` is found, then function converts it to eth curve pool.

This is incorrect, because attacker can manipulate price inside the pool using flashloan and then use that in order to mint more shares or withdraw more shares from strategy. In both cases it will loss of funds for other stakers.
## Tools Used
VsCode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Don't use pool price for conversion.





## Assessed type

Error

issues.title: AaveStrategy doesn't withdraw aave from stkAave in emergency
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L209-L219


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
AaveStrategy doesn't withdraw aave from stkAave in emergency
## Proof of Concept
`AaveStrategy` deposits user's funds into `LendingPool`.
During the time `AaveStrategy` earns rewards inside `incentivesController`, which [can be claimed](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L141-L143). These rewards are automatically staked into `stkAave`, so strategy `stkAave` balance is increasing during the time.

Also strategy always [changes `cooldown`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L172), which is needed to be able to unstake aave from stkAave.

But the problem is that `stkAave` balance is never considered as balance of all stakers.
And even [in emergency withdraw](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-yieldbox-strategies-audit/blob/05ba7108a83c66dada98bc5bc75cf18004f2a49b/contracts/aave/AaveStrategy.sol#L209-L219) there is no any ability to unstake `aave` from `stkAave`. Function just claim rewards and withdraws everything from lending pool.
## Tools Used
VsCode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
First of all i believe that stkAave should also be distributed among stakers. That's why `_currentBalance` function is incorrect as it doesn't account that. And also i believe that at least `emergencyWithdraw` should have ability to unstake aave.


## Assessed type

Error

issues.title: Wrong value for liquidationMultiplier can cause loss of user collateral to liquidators
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/Market.sol#L77


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
liquidationMultiplier value is too big and can cause loss of funds

## Proof of Concept
We can see the value of liquidationMultiplier is set to a default value in `Market.sol`:

```solidity
uint256 public liquidationMultiplier = 12000; //12%
```

It is then used in the formula:
```solidity
uint256 denominator = ((10 ** ratesPrecision) -
    (collateralizationRate *
        ((10 ** ratesPrecision) + liquidationMultiplier)) /
    (10 ** ratesPrecision)) * (10 ** (18 - ratesPrecision));
```

And we can see ratesPrecision default value is 5:
```solidity
    uint256 internal constant FEE_PRECISION_DECIMALS = 5;
```

Which means the provided value for liquidationMultiplier is not 12% as intended but 120%, which can lead to loss of funds during liquidation

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use `1200` as default value for liquidationMultiplier


## Assessed type

Math

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The contract uses a constant named `FEE_PRECISION` to calculate the `feeAmount` for asset borrowing. However, the specific value of `FEE_PRECISION` is not provided, which could lead to inconsistent precision and unintended behaviors.

## Vulnerability Details

In the given code, the `feeAmount` is calculated as `(amount * borrowOpeningFee) / FEE_PRECISION`, where `amount` is the borrowed amount, and `borrowOpeningFee` is a constant representing the flat percentage fee charged for any borrow action.

The vulnerability lies in the absence of the exact value of `FEE_PRECISION`. If `FEE_PRECISION` has a value that does not align with the precision of the calculation (e.g., if it is smaller than expected), the `feeAmount` calculation may result in inaccurate or unexpected fees.

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLLendingCommon.sol#L63C6-L63C6

1. Incorrect Fee Calculation: Inconsistent precision might lead to incorrect fee calculations, causing borrowers to be charged the wrong amount of fees for borrowing assets.

2. Loss of Funds: If the fee calculation results in overcharging borrowers, they might lose more funds than intended, leading to financial losses and potential user dissatisfaction.

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L808-L810

# Vulnerability details

## code
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L808-L810

## Impact
In both Singularity and BigBang, liquidation reward does not guarantee flat base reward to liquidator as per documentation

## Proof of Concept
In the dynamic liquidation incentives section of docs:
https://docs.tapioca.xyz/tapioca/core-functions-explained/liquidations

>There is a linear decrease in the liquidator's rewards from a min of 1% to a max of 10%. This is in addition to the flat base reward of 10%.

It can be assumed that the flat base reward is the liquidationFee added here:
```solidity
uint256 amountWithBonus = borrowAmount +
    (borrowAmount * liquidationMultiplier) /
    FEE_PRECISION;
```

However later the `callerShare` effectively received by the liquidator is multiplying `amountWithBonus` by the `callerReward` factor:

```solidity
uint256 returnedShare = balanceAfter - balanceBefore;
(uint256 feeShare, uint256 callerShare) = _extractLiquidationFees(
    returnedShare,
    borrowShare,
    callerReward
);
```

We can see that the callerShare can be arbitrarily small, and no flat base reward as stated in the docs

## Tools Used

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/usd0/modules/USDOMarketModule.sol#L104-L132


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The function removeAsset in `BaseUSDO.sol` can be front-run leading to theft of user funds, by using the signatures provided by an honest user in the parameter `approvals`

## Proof of Concept
In the call `removeAsset`:

```solidity
function removeAsset(
    address from,
    address to,
    uint16 lzDstChainId,
    address zroPaymentAddress,
    bytes calldata adapterParams,
    ICommonData.ICommonExternalContracts calldata externalData,
    IUSDOBase.IRemoveAndRepay calldata removeAndRepayData,
    ICommonData.IApproval[] calldata approvals
) external payable;
```

We can see that the variables `from` and `to` are unbounded. A malicious user Alice cannot remove assets from an arbitrary account if funds are not approved, which is the purpose of the `approvals` parameters. 
This parameter allows a legitimate user Bob to grant approvals for his assets on the fly using signatures for permits.

However this means that Alice can front-run Bob's transactions, use the signatures he provided but change the `to` address, meaning the funds would be redirected to her account

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add another signature which checks the parameters the function `removeAsset` is called with, most importantly the receiver `to`


## Assessed type

MEV

issues.title: Users can't make transfer due to wrong login in MarketERC20.sol
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L128-L152


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Wrong logic of function transfer in MarketERC20.sol. In method 'transfer' have if condition

````
        // If `amount` is 0, or `msg.sender` is `to` nothing happens
        if (amount != 0 || msg.sender == to) {
            uint256 srcBalance = balanceOf[msg.sender];
            require(srcBalance >= amount, "ERC20: balance too low");
            if (msg.sender != to) {
                require(to != address(0), "ERC20: no zero address"); // Moved down so low balance calls safe some gas

                balanceOf[msg.sender] = srcBalance - amount; // Underflow is checked
                balanceOf[to] += amount;
            }
        }
````

In this condition if amount is not 0 or msg.sender IS to the condition is true and execute the code but the logic is wrong because code will be execute ONLY if msg.sender is 'to'. 

P.S. There have second if condition if (msg.sender != to) but because upper condition is msg.sender == to the execution of the code can't go to second condition because msg.sender will not be to.

## Proof of Concept
If msg.sender is not equal 'to' then transfer can't be executed. 
This mean that nobody can't send transfer if is not send to address from where is send to. 

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Need to change if condition from:
```
if (amount != 0 || msg.sender == to)
```
To: 
```
if (amount != 0 || msg.sender != to)
```


## Assessed type

ERC20

## Impact
BaseTOFTStrategyModule.strategyWithdraw may send wrong amount of funds to user

## Proof of Concept
`BaseTOFTStrategyModule.strategyWithdraw` is used to trigger withdraw from strategy on other chain and receive funds on yours chain.
User can provide `_amount` and `_share` params to this function.
Both of them [are passed to the `yieldBox.withdraw`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/modules/BaseTOFTStrategyModule.sol#L247).

The problem is that in case if both `amount` and `share` is provided to the `yieldBox.withdraw`, then it will use `share` and will [withdraw amount that corresponds to `share` value](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/YieldBox/blob/f5ad271b2dcab8b643b7cf622c2d6a128e109999/contracts/YieldBox.sol#L285).

So in case if `share` amount provided by user corresponds to bigger amount of assets, then `amount` provided by user, then function will [send less amount to user](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapiocaz-audit/blob/bcf61f79464cfdc0484aa272f9f6e28d5de36a8f/contracts/tOFT/modules/BaseTOFTStrategyModule.sol#L217) and rest of payment will stay in `BaseTOFTStrategyModule` contract.

Example.
1.User provide amount 0, and share 100, because it's ok to use share instead of amount in yieldbox.
2.Contract withdraws 100 shares from yieldbox, but sends 0 amount to user on another chain.
3.User lost funds.
## Tools Used
VsCode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
`yieldbox.withdraw` returns how many assets were withdrawn. Use it to send correct amount to initiator.

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/main/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L535


# Vulnerability details

The protocol's option issuance is tied to the issuance of new TapOFT tokens, which is pausable by the conservator.

## Impact
Users enter new option positions by issuing oTAP NFTs, which is later converted into TapOFT OFT20 tokens. When they attempt to exit, they must call [`exerciseOption()`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/main/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L351), the contract proceeds to call [`_processOTCDeal()`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/main/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L395) and then [`extractTAP()`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/main/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L535). [But there's a pause modifier in this function](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/tokens/TapOFT.sol#L220), which means users will be forced to hold their position for the duration of the pause, possibly into expiry if the epoch ends before the contract resumes it's service. Given the volatile nature of tokens prices (one could also argue given their price reaction to news), an user who may wish to exercise an option at a more favorable moment can be forced to hold until it's OTM, leaving them with a loss of system origin. 

Notice the pause function does not pause the issuance of oTAP positions (can be found [here](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/main/contracts/options/TapiocaOptionBroker.sol#L212)), meaning more clueless users could enter positions they're unaware they cannot exit.

## Proof of Concept

1) New epoch begins on a tuesday
2) User mints oTAP, holds
3) System is paused on a thursday
4) Price surges for the duration of 3 days
5) User is unable to exercise their option at a favorable period
6) Price dives down, option is now OTM and it expires

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Public function that approves an user controlled target and amount. The function seems to be internal called by `borrow`, but the devs forgot to put the internal keyword and they put the public one. That means anyone can call the function with a fake `borrowParams` and drain the whole contract and the one who inherits from him (if any).

## Proof of Concept
It's a classic lack of access control of a critical function, I won't deepen more.

```
function borrowInternal( <==================================== HERE the name says it all
        bytes32 _to,
        ITapiocaOFT.IBorrowParams memory borrowParams,
        ICommonData.IWithdrawParams memory withdrawParams,
        ICommonData.IApproval[] memory approvals
    ) public payable { <======================================= HERE but it is public
        if (approvals.length > 0) {
            _callApproval(approvals);
        }

        // Use market helper to deposit, add collateral to market and withdrawTo
        approve(address(borrowParams.marketHelper), borrowParams.amount); <======================== HERE user controlled dest address and amount 
        IMagnetar(borrowParams.marketHelper)
            .depositAddCollateralAndBorrowFromMarket{value: msg.value}(
            borrowParams.market,
            LzLib.bytes32ToAddress(_to),
            borrowParams.amount,
            borrowParams.borrowAmount,
            true,
            true,
            withdrawParams
        );
    }

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L309-L326

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
BigBang.liquidate and SGLLiquidation.liquidate have only 1 swap data param for different swaps. As swap data is used to retrieve min amount after swap, liquidator can't provide slippage for all trades.

## Proof of Concept
Liquidator can liquidate several users in same time using [`liquidate` function](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L309-L326). Pls, note that liquidator provides one `swapper` and 1 `collateralToAssetSwapData`. But he provides arrays for users and their debts.

Later, this `collateralToAssetSwapData` will be used [to fetch `minAssetMount`](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L605) that liquidator wants to receive from the swap.
Because, `collateralToAssetSwapData` is not array, that means that user can provide only same min amount for all trades, which is not correct.
Because of that liquidators will have to use big min amout, to not revert all calls or do liquidations only for 1 user a time.
## Tools Used
VsCode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Allow liquidator to provide array of min amounts.

Error

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L560-L637


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
BigBang._liquidateUser doesn't burn liquidated USDO and creates insolvency.

## Proof of Concept
When user is going to be liquidated, then his debt that can be liquidated in USDO and collateral amount that can be spent [is calculated](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L582-L586).

This actually means, that `collateralShare` amount should be traded in order to cover `borrowPart` of USDO that is held by owner.
When [swap is done](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L618) then swapped USDO is received by `BigBang`. Then liquidator and protocol receive their fees [from extra shares](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L644).

Nothing else is done in the `_liquidateUser` function.
The problem is that total borrow amount of USDO [is decreased](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L822-L823), but liquidated part was not burnt.
As result, this amount is still present in total circulation of USDO, but it's not backed by collateral anymore.
And also as this amount is inside contract it [is assumed to be protocol fee](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L446), which is wrong.

Burn liquidated USDO amount.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
An attacker can steal user's collateral by frontrunning their `addCollateral()` transaction.
If the user for whatever reason would set an infinite approval on the collateral token on the market the attacker can steal all their collateral tokens at any time.

This is true for both BigBang and Singularity markets.

## Vulnerability Detail
When a user adds collateral to the Bigbang and Singularity markets they call the `addCollateral()` function. There are 2 scenarios; either by sending the tokens directly to the market and calling `addCollateral()`  with the `skim` set to `true` or by first approving the contract and then calling `addCollateral()` with `skim` set to `false` in which case an approval/sendFrom scheme is used. 
In both scenarios however there is no check between the `to` address and the `msg.sender` meaning  the call to `addCollateral()` can be front run by an attacker that specifies the `to` address as their own,

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L282-L290


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
BigBang.addCollateral allows to add any amount on behalf of owner without allowance. Any user can steal funds.

## Proof of Concept
`BigBang.addCollateral` function can be used to add collateral on behalf of owner.
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L282-L290
```solidity
    function addCollateral(
        address from,
        address to,
        bool skim,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 share
    ) public allowedBorrow(from, share) notPaused {
        _addCollateral(from, to, skim, amount, share);
    }
```
There are `share` and `amount` params that caller can provide. In case if `share` param is 0, then `amount` [is converted to shares](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L550-L552).

`addCollateral` function can be called on behalf of owner. That's why `allowedBorrow(from, share)` modifier is called to check allowance. The problem is that caller can provide 0 as `share` and as result he will always pass allowance. Because of that he can spend any amount of `from` that is approved to `BigBang`. For example, he can add this collateral to himself using `to` param.
## Tools Used
VsCode
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Check approval when you have calculated shares.
