MagnetarV2.sol)

## Proof of Concept
The issue here is clear

```
// in _withdraw function, line 753
    ...
    uint256 gas = msg.value > 0 ? msg.value : address(this).balance; <====================== HERE
    _withdrawToChain(
            yieldBox,
            from,
            withdrawCollateral ? market.collateralId() : market.assetId(),
            withdrawOnOtherChain ? destChain : 0,
            receiver,
            amount,
            share,
            adapterParams,
            gas > 0 ? payable(msg.sender) : payable(this),
            gas
    );
}
```

The avaiable gas is put to the balance of the contract if there is no `msg.value` before doing the withdraw, so that a malicious `receiver` contract that implements a callback function can, for example, `while(i <= 1e10) {sstore(...)}`, consuming all the gas but letting enough to return correctly, can drain all the funds inside the `MagnetarMarketModule` (if `withdrawOnOtherChain=false`, then it is exploitable on the current chain). 

It may be possible to exploit such a flaw between calls to other chains but there is no need to POC that, the point here is clear:

- Do NOT put the whole balance of a contract as gas in a transaction to untrusted destinations

Manual analysis

Set a limit for gas expenditure and revert if the user did not provided any/enough (or, at least, do not put the whole balance of the contract as gas). Just add something like

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The `getTotalDebt` function may return a smaller value than it should. This error directly impacts the debt rate computation of non-eth markets. 

Non-eth markets compute their debt rate based on the total debt of the eth market. For example, a target debt for the BNB market might be 50% of the ETH market. The debt rate increases when the debt of the BNB market approaches this value up to the `maxDebtRate` and decreases in the opposite direction down to `minDebtRate`. 

The ETH market debt must be correctly computed for this mechanism to work properly. Hence, ensuring that `getTotalDebt` returns the correct value is important.

## Proof of Concept

The `getTotalDebt` is supposed to return the total debt of the system. Currently is implemented as follows:

```solidity
function getTotalDebt() external view returns (uint256) {

}

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L232-L234


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.
Anybody can call ``BigBang.accrue()`` and realize a compound interest rate instead of a simple interest rate. The main issue is that ``BigBang.accrue()`` has no access control and then ``BigBang.accrue()`` calls ``_accrue()``,  which adds the new interest to the principal immediately. 

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

``BigBang.accrue()`` has no access control and anybody can call it to accrue interest: 

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L232-L234](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L232-L234)

In term, ``BigBang.accrue()`` calls ``_accrue()`` to calculate the elapsed time and the new interest charge. 

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L512-L541](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/bigBang/BigBang.sol#L512-L541)

The function calculates the new interest into ``extraAmount`` and then add it to the principal ``_totalBorrow.elastic`` immediately. As a result, the function realizes a compound interest rate based on the frequency of the call of ``BigBang.accrue()``.

A user can exploit this to call  ``BigBang.accrue()`` frequently and charge more interests than expected. 


## Tools Used
VSCode

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Introduce a new variable ``_totalBorrow.interest`` for interests and only accrue the interest to this variabl

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L361-L367


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.
twTAP.claimAndSendRewards() will claim the wrong amount for each reward token due to the use of wrong index. As a result, some users will lose some rewards and others will claim more rewards then they deserve. 

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

twTAP.claimAndSendRewards() allows the tapOFT to claim and send a list of rewards indicated in ``_rewardTokens``.

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L361-L367](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L361-L367)

It calls the function `` _claimRewardsOn()`` to achieve this: 

[https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L499-L519](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tap-token-audit/blob/59749be5bc2286f0bdbf59d7ddc258ddafd49a9f/contracts/governance/twTAP.sol#L499-L519)

Unfortunately, at L509, it uses the index of ``i`` instead of the correct index of ``claimableIndex``. As a result, the amount that is claimed and transferred for each reward is wrong.

issues.title: Use of deprecated Chainlink function latestAnswer without validation
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/oracle/implementations/ARBTriCryptoOracle.sol#L117
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-periph-audit/blob/023751a4e987cf7c203ab25d3abba58f7344f213/contracts/oracle/implementations/SGOracle.sol#L51


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Chainlink oracle data feed is not sufficiently validated and can return stale price.

## Proof of Concept
First problem is that, The ARBTriCryptoOracle.sol#L117._get(), is calling latestAnswer to get the last price for assets. According to Chainlink's documentation, the latestAnswer function is deprecated. 

This function does not revert if no answer has been reached but returns 0. Also, no price validation has been done. There is no check for price is more than 0 and stale price and round completeness. Price can be stale and can lead to wrong answer return value.
https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/api-reference#latestanswer

Also, the Tapioca protocol is intended for use in Arbitrum L2. 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-07-tapioca#tests

based on the chainlink docs, it is also required to check if the sequencer is down to avoid prices from looking like they are fresh although they are not.
https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/using-data-feeds
https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds

## Tools Used
Manually

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use latestRoundData function. Calling latestRoundData allow you to run some extra validations such as stale price and round completeness. 

In Arbitrum, Add check to make sure the sequencer is alive before using the oracle data


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLCommon.sol#L55
https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/singularity/SGLCommon.sol#L104


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The fullAssetAmount value, is updated with out of date _totalBorrow.elastic value. the result is wrong value for the fullAssetAmount, feeFraction, utilization.

## Proof of Concept
The fullAssetAmount value, is calculating by below formula, at line SGLCommon.sol#L55.

        uint256 fullAssetAmount = yieldBox.toAmount(
            assetId,
            _totalAsset.elastic,
            false
        ) + _totalBorrow.elastic;

The problem is that, it is using out of date _totalBorrow.elastic value. _totalBorrow.elastic value is updated at line SGLCommon.sol#L104.

        // Accrue interest
        extraAmount =
            (uint256(_totalBorrow.elastic) *
                _accrueInfo.interestPerSecond *
                elapsedTime) /
            1e18;
        _totalBorrow.elastic += uint128(extraAmount);

The fullAssetAmount, is used to calculate feeFraction and utilization. the result is wrong value for the fullAssetAmount, feeFraction, utilization.

## Tools Used
Manually

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Move below code to line SGLCommon.sol#L105, after _totalBorrow.elastic += uint128(extraAmount).

        uint256 fullAssetAmount = yieldBox.toAmount(
            assetId,
            _totalAsset.elastic,
            false
        ) + _totalBorrow.elastic;


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L135-L199


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In general, this integer underflow/overflow vulnerability can lead to serious security issues and unexpected behavior like loss of funds or data corruption.

## Proof of Concept
The following parts are affected by the vulnerability of integer underflow/overflow:

1/ **transfer()** function [LINK](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L135-L152): The subtraction operation **balanceOf[msg.sender] - amount** in the **transfer** function can result in an underflow if the **amount** is greater than the **balanceOf[msg.sender]** value. This can lead to a negative balance or even wrap around to a large positive balance.

2/ **transferFrom()** function [LINK](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L159-L187): Similar to the **transfer** function, the subtraction operation **balanceOf[from] - amount** in the **transferFrom** function can result in an underflow if the **amount** is greater than the **balanceOf[from]** value. This can lead to a negative balance or wrap around to a large positive balance.

3/ **approve()** function [LINK](https://github.com/Tapioca-DAO/tapioca-bar-audit/blob/2286f80f928f41c8bc189d0657d74ba83286c668/contracts/markets/MarketERC20.sol#L193-L199): Although not directly related to the vulnerability, the allowance management in the **approve** function can be impacted indirectly. If an overflow occurs when adding to the **allowance[from][msg.sender]** variable, it can result in an unintended increase in the allowance, allowing an attacker to spend more tokens than intended.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1- Bounds Checking: Add bounds checking to ensur

Hello Team,


## What is Precision Loss issue ( Divide before Multiply) :

Solidity uses a fixed-point number system, where the data type and the number of decimal places are predetermined. During an arithmetic operation involving floating-point numbers, the result of the code execution may not be accurate due to the limited precision of the fixed-point system. These can cause unexpected behavior in the smart contract functionality, such as rounding errors or arithmetic overflow and underflow conditions that can manifest itself through a huge loss of funds.
